summary: [Horn Diplomat] Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, Oct. 22, 2026 (Horndiplomat -- Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed visited the Ethiopian Nuclear Energy Commission to review progress in developing the country's nuclear energy programme, highlighting the role of advanced technology in Ethiopia's long-term economic transformation.

title: Ethiopia Records Tangible Progress in Building Sustainable, Healthy Food System
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is transforming its agricultural sector to deliver affordable, healthy food, create jobs and protect natural resources, Ethiopian Agricultural Transformation Institute (ATI) Director General Mandefro Nigussie said.

title: Fighting in Border Town Moyale Spreads to Three More Districts, Exchange of Heavy Gunfire
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- What started as a dispute over the raising of a Somali Regional State flag in Moyale town, Borana Zone, Oromia Region, followed by the killing of a 13-year-old girl on October 18, has escalated into sustained fighting, with security forces from the Oromia and Somali regions exchanging heavy gunfire.

title: Peace Over Rivalry - Somalia's Future Lies in Cooperation, Not Confrontation With Ethiopia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Somalia needs a foreign policy that gives its people a better chance of living in peace. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud should place cooperation with Ethiopia at the center of that effort while protecting Somalia's sovereignty and maintaining its wider international partnerships. With so much unfinished work at home, Mogadishu cannot afford to let other governments' rivalries determine its relationship with its largest neighbor.

title: Ethiopia's Coffee Sector Faces $453 Million Export Risk Under EU Deforestation Rules
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia could lose up to $453 million in coffee export revenue under the European Union's deforestation regulation, with compliance gaps threatening to exclude smallholder farmers from a market that accounts for around 30% of the country's coffee exports, according to an October 2026 briefing paper by ODI Global.

title: Drone Strikes Kill Schoolchildren in Amhara, Civilians in Tigray Regions As Conflicts Show No Sign of Abating
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Drone strikes in Ethiopia's Amhara and Tigray regions killed schoolchildren and other civilians on Tuesday, 20 October, according to eyewitnesses and local residents who spoke to Addis Standard, adding to mounting civilian casualties amid renewed fighting between federal forces and armed opponents in both regions.

title: Ethiopia's Abiy Ahmed Honours Kenya's National Heroes
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Nairobi, Kenya -- Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed paid tribute to Kenya's freedom fighters and national heroes during Mashujaa Day celebrations in Eldoret on Tuesday, highlighting the two countries' shared history of struggle, sacrifice and national unity.

title: Who Protects the Protectors? Inside the Growing Danger for Ethiopia's Humanitarian Workers
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- When humanitarian workers travel to the field, they carry more than food, medicine, or information. They carry the hopes of people facing hunger, displacement, illness, and conflict. Yet, the danger increasingly exposes those delivering this assistance.

title: Obituary - Prominent Kenyan Oromo Scholar, Anthropologist Professor Abdullahi Shongolo Passes Away
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Professor Abdullahi Shongolo, a prominent scholar of history and anthropology whose research on Borana Oromo culture, customary law, and history brought international attention to the community's rich heritage, passed away on 20 October at the age of 68 at Nanyuki Hospital in Kenya, following an illness from which he did not recover.

title: Entrenched Authoritarianism: Ethiopia's Rule of Law Index Slides Further
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia's rule of law performance has deteriorated further, with the country ranking 133rd out of 143 countries and jurisdictions in the 2026 World Justice Project (WJP) Rule of Law Index, according to the ranking provided for this report. The latest assessment extends a multi-year decline that has seen the country remain near the bottom of global and sub-Saharan African comparisons.

title: News - 13-Year-Old Girl Killed After Flag Dispute in Borana's Moyale - Protesters Block Transport Services
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The opening of a new Somali Region administration office and the raising of its flag in Moyale town in Borana zone of Oromia regional state on October 18 triggered an exchange of gunfire between Somali regional forces and Oromia local militias, leaving a 13-year-old girl dead and prompting protests that disrupted transport services and forced businesses to close on Monday, residents told Addis Standard.

title: PM Abiy Warns Eritrea of 'Extremely Severe' Consequences If It Rejects Peace Call
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has warned Eritrea of "extremely severe" consequences if its government continues to reject Ethiopia's calls for peace and regional cooperation, accusing Asmara of aligning itself with forces seeking to destabilize Ethiopia. He also called on Tigrayan youth to abandon armed struggle, accusing Tigrayan People's Liberation Front (TPLF) leaders of prolonging conflict at the expense of the region's population.

title: Ethiopia Warns Somaliland Recognition Could Strengthen Al-Shabaab, Somaliland Officials Push Back
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia has warned that recognizing Somaliland could undermine regional counterterrorism efforts and strengthen Al-Shabaab, while Somaliland officials have rejected the security concerns, arguing that recognition would instead enhance regional stability and advance Ethiopia's economic and strategic interests.

summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A group of Oromo intellectuals and public figures has backed the Oromo Liberation Army's (OLA) participation in a newly formed opposition coalition that includes the Amhara Fano movement, describing the alliance as a potential opening to address Ethiopia's deepening political crisis while calling for an inclusive transition that safeguards the rights and political aspirations of all communities.

title: Ghana Set to Overtake Ethiopia As Africa's Eighth-Largest Economy After Kenya Takes East Africa Lead
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ghana is projected to overtake Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy in 2026, with its gross domestic product (GDP) forecast to reach US$128.64 billion, exceeding Ethiopia's projected US$127.15 billion by US$1.49 billion, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO), as reported by African Business Insider on 17 October.
